comments.note: Tag.cs: The computed Importance and NameWithPath properties have non-required init defaults (Unused and empty string). Consumers using 'required' positional record construction will get the defaults unless TagsManager explicitly sets them via 'with {}'. This is correct per the design — just worth noting for future consumers that these fields are populated post-construction by TagsManager, not by the DB mapper.

comments.note: TaggingOptions.MostUsedThreshold has no range validation (valid domain is 1–5, matching TagImportance). Values of 0, negative, or >5 would produce silently wrong behaviour in the future TagsManager. Consider adding a guard in TagsManager rather than in the options record, per the constraints 'only validate at system boundaries'.

Tag.NameWithPath defaults to string.Empty if TagsManager fails to set it (e.g., partial collection init). Downstream UI consumers relying on hierarchical display would receive silent empty strings. This is a future concern for TagsManager's caller contract, not a defect in the record itself.
